articleTitle: On the Dynamic Response of Static Var Compensators in Faulted Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper assesses the performance of static var compensators (SVC) connected to power systems during short-circuits and reclosing procedures. The long transmission line used for simulations interconnects two substations in Brazil, which are close to the wind and photovoltaic parks. The real parameters-based 500 kV power system is modeled in the EMTP-RV software, as well as the distance function-based relay. The SVC is connected at a terminal of the transmission line, and it is composed of a thyristor-controlled reactor (TCR) and thyristor-switched capacitors (TSC). The power system is then submitted to short-circuits mainly with different types and fault resistances, as well as to single-pole and three-pole reclosing scenarios. This work then allows to visualize in detail the sequence of the control scheme by analyzing the susceptance, the firing angle of the TCR, and the logic states of TSCs. From the results, it is demonstrated that the type of fault and reclosing, depending on the number of faulted phases, as well as the transmission line loading and fault resistance, are relevant factors to modify the SVC response. In addition, the simulations demonstrate that the SVC may be submitted to severe efforts in the case of three-pole reclosing of transmission lines once the reactive power to be delivered is higher if compared with the single-pole reclosing procedure, reaching even its operation limits. Finally, this kind of study could help to define the best alternative to switching the transmission lines during faults watching out for the lifetime of the compensation equipment. This evaluation may be relevant, especially in renewable resources-penetrated power systems where these power electronic devices could be allocated.

articleTitle: Computational Tool for Assessing and Comparing Indoor Localization Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper presents a computational tool designed to evaluate and compare various indoor localization methods. Recognizing the inherent limitations of satellite visibility in specific areas, this study explores alternative techniques for indoor localization, such as Received Signal Strength Indicator, Angle-of-Arrival, Time-of-Arrival, and Time-Difference-of-Arrival. Employing meticulous measurement and estimation procedures, the tool aims to provide reliable solutions for indoor positioning, with an educational focus in mind. Through the comprehensive evaluation of diverse indoor localization methods, the paper endeavors to identify the most effective and precise approaches under different parameters. This not only benefits professionals and academics in the field but also supports the learning and understanding of students interested in the development of advanced indoor positioning systems.

articleTitle: Prediction of Telecommunications Customer Churn Based on Hybrid Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of customer churn in the telecommunications sector by proposing a hybrid model that integrates Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. Fourteen models were evaluated, including eight individual and six hybrid models, using a public Kaggle dataset across two different scenarios. In the scenario without feature selection, the individual LGBM and XGB models excelled with accuracies of 97.7%, while the hybrid model combining XGB, SVM and RF stood out by achieving a 99.12% accuracy. In the scenario with feature selection, the individual LGBM and XGB models reached an accuracy of 97%, but the hybrid model of XGB, SVM and RF improved to 98.4%. These results surpass several models described in prior literature, demonstrating a significant improvement in churn prediction and providing telecommunications companies with an advanced tool for retaining their customers.

articleTitle: Hardening to Improve the Security of Financial Institutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The great importance of having financial institutions certified in PCI DSS is the generation of a security environment in terms of data protection and it is an incentive that positions financial institutions as professional, responsible, serious and reliable. This research work proposes the implementation of hardening techniques and the application of security methodologies that allow having an advanced level of security in order to reduce vulnerabilities and risks that may exist in financial institutions. Previously, articles referring to security methodologies and standards applied in different case studies were reviewed in order to have a reference and be able to apply them in our case study. The proposed methodology is composed of 5 stages 1) Information gathering, in which information mapping was carried out. 2) Vulnerability Analysis, performing the scanning of the network in the productive area. 3) Application and comparison of information security methodologies, which include: PCI DSS, OSSTMM v3, OWASP and the following scanning tools were used: Nmap, Xprobe 2, Wireshark, Netstat, etc. 4) Analysis of the results. 5) Report generation. The results of the study indicate a 2 improvement in the effectiveness of mitigated risks and controls. On the other hand, when comparing security methodologies, the PCI DSS standard scores better on the comparison scale for our case study, as it is closely aligned with internal banking processes (SMEs).

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Cost Non-Invasive Modular Kit for Wheelchair Motorization in Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Wheelchairs are essential for people with reduced mobility. Motorization of these devices can provide an increase quality of living and independence for their users. However, the cost of electric wheelchairs makes them inaccessible to users from developing countries. To address this issue, a low-cost modular kit is proposed, designed and manufactured. The mechatronic design of the kit includes the mechanical design of the components as well as dimensioning, the selection of electronic components, as well as the incorporation of IoT technology to be able to control it using a smartphone if necessary. The resulting modular kit proves to be useful as it can be rapidly installed on a commercial wheelchair without modifying its structure. Preliminary tests of the functional prototype show the wheelchair can provide enhanced mobility to the user, a low turning radius for narrow spaces, as wells as the ability to easily climb up and down on ramps.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of LoRa Propagation Models for IoT Applications in Lima, Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of a LoRa-based data transmission system deployed across urban, suburban, and outdoor areas in Lima, Peru. The study highlights signal reliability challenges, particularly in dense urban environments where high-rise buildings and infrastructure cause significant attenuation and interference. Results show robust performance in outdoor settings, while urban areas required further analysis to address signal loss. The research applies and adapts Okumura-Hata propagation models, proposing new equations tailored to Lima's specific geographic and structural conditions. These equations provide a more accurate prediction of signal behavior in urban environments, guiding strategies for optimizing LoRa networks. Future work will explore solutions such as increased node density and repeaters to improve coverage without extensive infrastructure modifications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Security Controls for the Treatment of Malware Using Breach and Attack Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Currently there is a significant increase in cyber-attacks associated with increased access to the digital world, where every company focuses its efforts on becoming digitally transformed. The systems present new vulnerabilities that put at risk key assets and sensitive data and where the need to implement better and more effective security controls to protect this valuable resource is born. This paper proposes the use of an architectural model with security controls aligned to NIST standards, using Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS) technologies to improve threat detection in real time and increase the effectiveness of these controls. To this end, security tools such as EDR, WAF, IPS and IDS were implemented in a controlled simulation environment, under NIST standards and using BAS as a key technology. With this architecture we obtained an improvement in the analysis and detection times of threats, with an effectiveness of 80% in detection, protecting the IT infrastructure and the commercial image of the companies in which it was implemented, with which it was possible to determine that the proposed model optimized the protection of assets through the timely detection of threats and an increase in the efficiency of security controls.

articleTitle: Kinematic Control for the Motion Generation of Robot Manipulators Using MoMask LLM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In recent years, numerous Large Language Models have been developed, offering a wide variety of applications. Among these, motion generation for 3D human representations has gained attention due to its potential in simulations, animations, and video games. However, the application of LLMs to robot motion is still in its early stages. This paper presents the use of an LLM to generate motion for a robot manipulator simulated in RViz within ROS. We obtain human animated motion from a pre-trained LLM and retarget it to a manipulator robot in the task space, using as example the UR5 and Sawyer robots. This reference is then used as input to a nulls pace hierarchical kinematic controller that follows the hand and elbow motion. The results show that the proposed approach generates motion that resembles the movements of a human character, achieving a maximum error of 0.04 m for the UR5 and 0.03 m for the Sawyer Robot.

articleTitle: Development and Implementation of an Interoperable and Flexible Supervisory Software for a Power Electric System in a Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Automation solutions oriented towards power electrical systems (PES) in a smart grid predominantly employ a single brand. This causes difficulties when integrating new equipment. Additionally, monitoring is often tedious, leading to data misinterpretation and delays in preventive actions. This project presents a smart grid through the connection of 3 power generation stations and a consumption station to an Orion LX centralizer and a supervisory computer. Siemens Power Meters and Lucas Nulle collector bars are used. The equipment communicates via the Modbus TCPIIP protocol, and Lab View is used for the development of the supervisory software.

articleTitle: Modelling and LQG/LTR Control of a Propelled AUV in Longitudinal Dynamic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The development of underwater vehicles considers main areas of modelling, navigation, guidance and control. The autonomous underwater vehicles have been modified in order to improve the maneuverability and to be applied in local inspection tasks, such as remotely operated vehicles. The current paper investigates the modelling and control of an AUV composed of four propellers, stabilizing fins and without control surfaces. The modelling is developed following the slender body theory, obtaining the longitudinal hydrodynamic coefficients. The LQG/LTR robust control approach is applied to control the surge and pitch rate dynamics. The pitch attitude dynamics in uncontrollable directly by a centralized controller, then a PID in cascade structure is proposed to tack this problem. The results achieve the desired performance in rising and diving maneuvers.

articleTitle: Real-Time Wireless Centralized Control of the Level-Temperature Process in a Multipurpose Tank
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In this work, a centralized MIMO (Multiple-Input Multiple-Output) integer-order control and a centralized MIMO fractional-order control, both wireless, are implemented in order to simultaneously control the water level and temperature of the upper tank in a multipurpose plant located in the Automation Laboratory of the University of Engineering and Technology (UTEC), in Peru. For the implementation of the wireless control systems, Siemens SCALANCE W774 and W734 devices were used, which operated with the Profinet communication protocol. The results obtained in the experiments demonstrate that the fractional-order centralized control approach exhibits better performance in level control compared to the integer-order centralized control approach, especially in terms of overshoot percentage and settling time. Regarding temperature control, the fractional-order centralized control approach shows a lower overshoot percentage and a lower steady-state error. However, in terms of settling time, the integer-order centralized control was better compared to its fractional counterpart.

articleTitle: Implementation of Vector Speed Control in a Split-Winding Three-Phase Bearingless Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study presents the implementation of a vector control strategy for speed in a bearingless three-phase induction motor with split winding using a four-arm inverter. The objective is to ensure a fast speed response, even under high torque in both transient and steady-state regimes. The method performance is analyzed and validated with experimental results.

articleTitle: Design of a Low-Cost Social Robot for Automated Triage in Primary Care
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In Peru's healthcare system, effective triage is crucial for categorizing patients according to the severity of their conditions and the urgency of required care. However, challenges such as limited resources, inadequate infrastructure, and a shortage of adequately trained medical personnel often result in suboptimal patient management. To mitigate these challenges, this study proposes the implementation of a social robot aimed at enhancing triage efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Machine Learning Methods for Fault Classification in Electric Systems with Distributed Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The continued growth of Distributed Energy Resources (DER) presents challenges to electrical grids, not the least of which is electrical protection. This article develops a classification criterion to identify the fault zone in a distribution network using some well-known machine learning methods on transient RMS signals. The signals considered are: active power, reactive power, voltage, current and frequency extracted from the Power Plant Controller (PPC) of the distribution generator inverter. Then, this information is part of the input for different classification methods to evaluate their efficiency, this by simulating different fault cases. The simulations were performed on a generic model obtained from Power Factory, while the analysis for testing and training was performed in Matlab. The results show that the multilayer perceptron method gives better results.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Water Level Controller in Pumping Chamber which is Part of a Wastewater Treatment Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article presents the implementation of a level control system for the drainage pumping station (CBD-01) at the wastewater treatment plant (PTAR) in the city of Cusco, Peru. The control system is based on a PID controller, where the controlled variable is the water level in the pumping chamber, and the manipulated variable is the rotational speed of four pumps, regulated through variable frequency drives (VFD), with the aim of maintaining a constant water level below the overflow point. To achieve this, an OPC connection was established between the PLC and Matlab software, allowing for data acquisition from the open-loop process. Subsequently, the estimated parameters for the PID controller were calculated using the Lambda tuning method, which is suitable for processes with non-self-regulating behavior (integrating processes). The PID controller was implemented in the PLC of the pumping station, and after experimental tests, the controller parameters were adjusted, resulting in final gains of Kc = 15, Ti = 4.5, and Td = 0, with rise and settling times of 70 and 75 seconds, respectively, without significant overshoot or harmful oscillations in the steady state. The results showed a fast and stable response to changes in the setpoint or disturbances in the system.

articleTitle: Transmission Loss Analysis of Indoor Building Materials in the 24–30 GHz Frequency Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The new generations of mobile communications use radio waves with increasingly higher frequencies to provide greater bandwidth, thereby offering users higher transmission rates. However, these waves suffer greater attenuation as they propagate and also experience higher transmission or penetration losses due to materials found in the wireless channel. In this study, an analysis of the transmission loss of radio waves in the frequency range 2 (FR2), from 24 GHz to 30 GHz, in materials typically found in indoor building environments was conducted measuring the s21 parameter with a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) and two horn antennas. The materials considered were Medium Density Fibreboard (MDF), expanded polystyrene, glass, plywood, brick with tiles, drywall and metal. It was found that metal, as well as glass and MDF, exhibit the highest specific attenuation, while expanded polyestyrene is practically transparent to radio waves. Results can be used in predicting the coverage of beyond fifth generation mobile systems. The same methodology can be applied to measure the attenuation introduced by materials used to camouflage the new antennas that will operate in the millimeter band range.

articleTitle: Mobile Application for Pine Variety Classification in an Oxapampa Nursery Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Peru has large expanses of reforested hectares along its coast, with pine being one of the two most commonly used species for this practice. These plants originate from forest nurseries, which are centers for the reproduction and care of plants in their early stages of life before being transplanted to the field. A crucial stage in pine production is the classification of seeds by variety, which is fundamental for plant development. This influences the planting destination, subsequent care, and the transplant environment. In this article, we present a mobile application (app) for classifying pine seeds by variety. The app uses a model based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) designed to distinguish and predict among the Tecunumanii, Oocarpa, and Pseudostrobus pine varieties. The mobile application was built in three phases: Data Selection, Model Training, and Development and Implementation. The model achieved an accuracy of 90.32% in classifying pine seeds, demonstrating effectiveness and potential as a useful tool in managing the seed classification process in forest nurseries.

articleTitle: Effect of Prolonged Smartphone Use on Trapezius and Neck Extensor Muscle Activity Using sEMG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The intensive use of touchscreen mobile devices has been linked to musculoskeletal issues, articularly in the neck and shoulder regions, often referred to as “text-neck.” This study investigates the effects of prolonged smartphone use on the activity of the trapezius and sternocleidomastoid muscles in young adults (aged 20–25) using surface electromyography (sEMG). The primary aim is to evaluate muscle activity, head and neck posture during different tasks. The findings provide quantitative data on muscle activity during typical smartphone use, which can inform the development of targeted recommendations to mitigate the risk of pain and musculoskeletal injuries. The results emphasize the need for ergonomic solutions and preventive measures to address the musculoskeletal strain associated with smartphone use.

articleTitle: Design of a Medical Training Simulator for Laparoscopic Appendectomy with Haptic Grip and Touch Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This work develops the mechanical, electronic and control design of a simulator model with haptic feedback for laparoscopic appendectomy, with the purpose of improving laparoscopic surgical skills in a training environment. This system is designed so that the user will be able to visualize the virtual environment and its interaction with it through the screen. Learning to perform laparoscopic surgery requires environments and approaches that improve the dexterity in the handling of surgical instruments and optimize the practice, which are achieved with the presented system. The simulator employs haptic feedback, that is to say, the user will be able to have a realistic interaction with the tissues or internal organs. The system will: give feedback to the user with sensations to bring them closer to reality; simulate surgical equipment; and, reproduce an environment that accurately reflects the anatomy of the abdominal region surrounding the appendix. The user's progress data is recorded and displayed in real time. The mechanical design considers the analysis of designed components and their resistance in this work; the electronic design contemplates the selection of the electronic components as well as the image processing; and the control design considers the control strategy chosen for every part of the system controlled.

articleTitle: A Propelled AUV Simulator: A Case of Integration Between Gazebo Harmonic and ROS 2 Iron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The simulation of underwater vehicles provides a detailed view of their behavior, allowing us to validate their physical and hydrodynamic design, test control algorithms, and correct errors before implementation. This paper presents the methodology for the simulation of an autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV), named AIAPAEC, propelled by four thrusters, running on Gazebo Harmonic and ROS 2 Iron. Gazebo Harmonic simulates the three-dimensional behavior of the AUV using hydrodynamics, buoyancy, and thruster plugins, which replicate the AUV dynamics in an aquatic environment. In addition, the simulator provides the attitude, position, and velocities of the vehicle, based on the inertial measurement unit plugin, the odometry plugin, and the doppler velocity log plugin. The integration with ROS 2 Iron through ROS Gazebo Bridge allows the implementation of open-loop and closed-loop maneuvers. Five simulations are presented to verify simulator performance, validate control algorithms, and analyze the relationship between simulator frequency and Real Time Factor (RTF). The tests used an odometry sensor at 100 Hz, and IMU and DVL sensors at 10 Hz. The Gazebo base frequency was set to 1000 Hz and 100 Hz. Results from the on-off and MIMO controllers showed a good fit with the temporal responses. Finally, a performance comparison of the MIMO control simulation, with harmonic settings in Gazebo at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz, evaluated the impact on RTF using sensor sampling frequencies of 10 Hz for IMU and DVL, and 100 Hz for odometry.

articleTitle: Regression Ensemble Techniques Bagging, Gradient Boosting and XGBoost to Predict the Power of Photovoltaic Systems in the High Andean Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)

authors.preferredName: Jose Emmanuel Cruz De la Cruz

abstract: The production of electrical energy through the use of photovoltaic systems is very important, especially in the high Andean area and at altitudes above 3800 meters above sea level; knowing the phenomenon, managing it and being able to predict its behavior is very important to establish an electric energy management policy for the benefit of humanity. Ensemble techniques for regression such as Bagging, Gradient Boosting and XGBoost allow predictions of the power generated by photovoltaic systems based on predictor variables such as temperature, humidity, ultraviolet irradiance and illuminance. A photovoltaic monitoring system designed and implemented by the authors of this research has generated the dataset, it is possible to implement the same supervision system in other areas but only using the measurement of the predictor variables, without the need to implement the photovoltaic systems and determine the power thanks to the model generated by the ensemble techniques. The results show the lowest MSE using XGBoost with 4.1481, Bagging with Normalization has the second best MSE due to the simplicity of the technique. The lowest MAE is using XGBoost with 0.560257, the second lowest MAE is using Bagging with 0.577226. MAPE cannot be used because there are zero or close to zero values, and division by zero causes the MAPE value to tend to very high values. The best Score for the tests is XGBoost with 0.994991, very close are Bagging with Normalization and Gradient Boosting with Normalization.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Planar Array Antennas by Applying Tapering Techniques for LEO Satellite Communication Using MATLAB Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper presents a MATLAB-based approach to model a planar array antenna using the array factor. The proposed model allows the exploration of various tapering techniques and their impact on key radiation characteristics such as Side Lobe Level (SLL), directivity, and Half Power Beam Width (HPBW). The primary objective of this study is to assess the antenna's performance as a suitable solution for a Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication system. The study highlights the practical implications of the antenna's performance in LEO satellite deployment. The beam footprint, defining the coverage area on Earth's surface illuminated by the antenna's radiation pattern, is a critical consideration for effective communication and coverage capabilities. To validate the MATLAB-based method for antenna performance assessment, we designed a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30\ \times\ 30$</tex> planar array antenna using Ansys HFSS. Subsequently, we found that the simulation results from the antenna design in Ansys closely aligns with those obtained from the antenna modeling in MATLAB. In summary, this paper contributes a comprehensive analysis of a planar array antenna's radiation characteristics through various tapering techniques. By focusing on LEO satellite communication requirements, the study not only evaluates the antenna's efficacy but also demonstrates its suitability for real-world satellite applications, including its beam footprint and directional capabilities.

articleTitle: Distributed Photovoltaic Microgeneration Model to Improve Energy Efficiency in Residential Supplies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article presents the results of the research aimed at determining the influence of photovoltaic distributed microgeneration, with load profile variation on energy efficiency in residential supplies with BT5B tariff and consumption over 100kWh/month in the district of EI Tambo, province of Huancayo, Peru; the population consisted of all residential supplies of the district in question, the sample was a typical residential supply selected using non-probabilistic sampling by convenience because the research was conducted as an experimental type. The design and simulation of the results was carried out with the software “Perfilcargafv”, which was developed in Matlab; by means of this application and from the load profile of each supply, different profitable configurations of generation systems connected to the network can be obtained, analyzing each of the variables of the research. The results showed that the electrical energy consumed from the commercial network is considerably reduced, as well as the monthly billing, greenhouse gas emissions and energy losses; this allows concluding that the energy efficiency of residential supplies was significantly improved.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Population Exposure to Radiofrequency Fields in Microenvironments in the Cities of Lima, Cusco and Pucallpa in Perú, Using a Personal Exposimeter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The objective of this study was to make an evalu-ation of radiofrequency fields in microenvironments of Cuzco, Lima and Pucallpa using personal exposimeters. To carried it out a literature review was first made, then the urban environ-ments were defined, and 95 microenvironments were selected in the three cities. Subsequently, the exposimeter including the proprietary software for data processing was tested. In total, 1900 measurements of the main telecommunications services were carried out. The electric field was measured for each environment, with a maximum of 2.531 V/m, a minimum of 0.063 V/m and an average of 0.521 V/m for all measurements combined. Based on the ICNIRP 1998 limits, exposure quotients were also obtained for all the measurements combined and for the measurements in each city considering outdoor and indoor measurements, different types of environments and by main frequency bands. For all measurements combined, the maximum exposure quotient was 0.747% and the average was 0.033%. All measurements made were well below international limits, the largest contributors to total exposure were mobile phone base stations, the second largest were broadcasting services, and mobile phone handsets exposure was well below than that of mobile phone base stations.

articleTitle: Development of an Integrated Web Tool for Assessing the Energy Consumption and Carbon Footprint of the Photovoltaic Cycle: A New Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This research develops an integrated web-based tool to manage and analyze photovoltaic (PV) systems. The tool combines sizing, energy payback time (EPBT) and carbon footprint calculation. The current tools address these tasks separately and for different purposes, which results in less efficient and more labor-intensive processes. The development included an analysis of the sizing and life cycle of PV systems, the creation of a database with technical characteristics of polycrystalline solar panels, data for energy and carbon footprint calculations, and user data storage. The equations for these calculations were programmed, and the tool was validated by comparative testing with six existing studies, demonstrating its efficiency in reducing time and effort. It was found that energy production is highly dependent on annual irradiance. Furthermore, manufacturing and transport were identified as the largest consumers of energy in the PV cycle.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence and Industry: a bibliometrics analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing many fields of knowledge, especially in the field of industry. Thus, the need arises to systematize this information and identify research trends. Therefore, the objective of the study was to determine the current state of the documents that relate artificial intelligence and the industry. To do this, a bibliometric analysis of 4,858 investigations published in Scopus between 2019 and 2023 was carried out. It is found that the number of documents published in 2022 multiplies 10 times compared to 2019. A trend is observed to develop literature review studies. Likewise, IEEE Access magazine has the largest number of publications, but Sustainability magazine is the most cited. On the other hand, the affiliations come mainly from Asian countries, although their publications are in foreign magazines. Regarding co-authorship by country, it is found that the United States and China have the greatest influence in the field of study with an increasingly accessible and collaborative nature, especially with countries such as India and the United Kingdom, as well as the existence of a recurrence of research on topics such as industry 4.0, machine learning, decision making and the pharmaceutical industry.

articleTitle: Model to Predict Inventory Demand in Retail SMEs Using CRISP-DM and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study addresses efficient inventory management, a critical concern for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the retail sector, affecting their operational efficiency, cost management, and competitiveness. Despite its global prevalence, many SMEs lack efficient solutions that take advantage of available technology and information. The objective of this study is to train machine learning models to predict inventory demand in SMEs, addressing their unique challenges and limitations. The Cross Industry Standard Process for Data Mining methodology is employed to develop the model using four machine learning algorithms: Random Forest (RF), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Decision Tree (DT). The methodology consists of five phases: business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling and evaluation. For the training phase, cross-validation was used on a dataset consisting of 16,071 records collected from July 25, 2023 to March 29, 2024 from a Peruvian SME, considering a total of 14 variables. The results highlight XGBoost as the algorithm that best fit our records with an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.82.

articleTitle: Design of a Transtibial Prosthesis Prototype for Normal Walking Based on the Anatomical Measurements of an Average Peruvian Woman
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The demand for transtibial prostheses has increased in recent years. However, most active prostheses are designed for people who have larger and heavier body frames compared to other ethnic groups such as the Peruvian population. To address this limitation, this paper proposes the design of a prototype of active transtibial prosthesis for normal walking based on the anthropometric measurements and power requirements of the average Peruvian woman. The proposed prosthesis uses a motor-gear-ball screw mechanism, selecting the motor and ball screw on the basis of the torque and force requirements of the target individuals. We used the ANSI/AGMA methodology to choose the most adequate gears for the design. For the supports and structure that carry the entire weight of the individual, a mechanical simulation was performed to determine an adequate safety factor. In addition, a speed control simulation was added based on the designed mechanism. The results show the feasibility of our proposed design.

articleTitle: The Importance of an Optimal Integrated Operation of Electrical and Natural Gas Systems During Gas Rationing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Natural gas (NG) is a substantial supplier of electri-cal power systems (EPSs) due to its flexible dispatch. However, the strong dependence of the EPS power generation on NG leads the EPS to experience high operation costs and high Locational Marginal Prices (LMPs) whenever the NG supply is rationed in the EPS. To mitigate this adverse impact on the EPS, this work demonstrates that when NG supply is rationed, the short-term EPS operation optimization including natural gas network (NGN) constraints results in dispatch decisions that better coordinate hydro and gas resources and yield lower LMPs compared to the traditional EPS operation optimization without inclusion of NGN operation modeling. First, we introduce a hydrothermal unit commitment model that includes NGN operation constraints via Mix Integer Second Order Cone Programming. Second, we develop a publicly available real-world test system that models Peru's integrated EPS and NGN systems with high spatial resolution. We simulate the Peruvian integrated EPS and NGN system under realistic gas rationing. Simulations demonstrate that the integrated EPS and N G N operation optimization reveals a more efficient use of hydro and gas resources and a 14.5 % reduction in LMPs compared to a traditional unit commitment model that does not include NGN operation modeling. Moreover, we demonstrate that the high altitude of Peru's Andes grants a 121 % gain of gas pressure to Peru's NGN that results in a 12 % and 14.8% reduction in compressors gas consumption and LMPs, respectively, relative to the integrated EPS and NGN operation optimization that neglects Peru's Andes altitudes.

Author Keywords: Integrated electrical and natural gas systems

articleTitle: Evaluating Model Compression Techniques for On-Device Browser Sign Language Recognition Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Due to the improvement of sign language (SL) recognition models, more work has started to build upon them to create end-user platforms such as video-based dictionaries. Although most of them base their design on cloud services or APIs, this approach can become expensive, especially when working with such substantial dimensional data as videos. Other realities, such as regions with low internet connection and few economic resources, can benefit from the offline alternative for deploying these systems. However, models deployed in websites' front-end or edge devices have some constraints on their size. Therefore, our work evaluates two model compression techniques to enhance the performance of on-device inference for a SL recognition model. We test knowledge quantization and distillation on three datasets varied in size, ultimately deploying and evaluating them on a locally hosted web page. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first evaluation of a quantized and distilled transformer-based SL recognition model for on-device browser inference. Furthermore, the combination of both compression techniques achieves a size reduction of up to 17.83 times and a speedup of 5.9 times the baseline.

articleTitle: Dino Math Legacy: A Configurable Educational Video Game for Personalized Math Learning in Peruvian High Schools
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The use of educational video games has gained increasing popularity in recent years as a tool to enhance learning outcomes. However, there are still challenges in the way math is taught through video games, such as insufficient adaptation to diverse learning styles and limited flexibility in topic selection. These limitations have created a need for configurable video games that can be tailored to meet specific learning objectives while engaging students in an enjoyable and interactive manner. In response to the demand for more adaptable educational tools, this study introduces “Dino Math Legacy”, a customizable video game designed to reinforce math learning for first-year high school students, aligned with Peru's National Basic Education Curriculum. Teachers have the ability to tailor the game to specific learning goals, ensuring engagement through interactive and enjoyable experiences. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a video game in improving math learning for first-year high school students, focusing on its impact on engagement and learning outcomes. A mixed-methods evaluation confirmed the game's positive impact on learning outcomes and its successful integration of Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) principles, which enhance user experience and learning. Additionally, the study found that the game improved math learning by incorporating dynamic and interactive features, such as adaptive problem-solving challenges, tailored to individual learning styles. The game's customizable features allowed teachers to modify content and set specific learning objectives, which enhanced student motivation and improved comprehension of key math concepts. The research highlights the potential of educational video games in classroom learning, emphasizing the importance of aligning design with student learning styles. A user-centered design approach, guided by educational psychologists and frameworks like LEGA and LM-GM, ensured effectiveness. A comprehensive mixed-methods evaluation, incorporating both qualitative and quantitative analysis, validated the game's effectiveness in improving math learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Development of a Chatbot Powered by Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose and Improve Stress and Anxiety Levels in University Students
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Stress and anxiety among university students have become a significant issue, negatively impacting their academic performance and personal lives. To address this problem, an AI-powered chatbot was developed to provide personalized support based on Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) techniques. The chatbot offers multimodal interaction, cross-platform availability, and a user-centric design to enhance accessibility and engagement. An experiment was conducted with 47 Peruvian university students aged 19–26 to assess the chatbot's usability using the System Usability Scale (SUS). The results revealed an average SUS score of 82.13, indicating high usability compared to other digital health applications and chatbots, and promising stress and anxiety levels reduction, measured with the GAD-7 and PSS-14 surveys. The chatbot's effectiveness may vary among individuals, and ongoing research and optimization are necessary. However, this innovative solution demonstrates the potential of AI-driven chatbots in providing accessible mental health support for university students, contributing to their overall well-being and academic success.

articleTitle: Investigating Patterns and Associations of Different Cancer Types in Peru: A Data-driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study examines whether the incidence of the most common cancers in Peruvian society is associated with access to health services and socioeconomic individual characteristics. The aim was to investigate the relationship between common cancers, individual patient characteristics, health centre locations and the Human Development Index of Peruvian society. Data were obtained from the Peruvian Open Data Platform and provided by the Fondo Intangible Solidario de Salud (FISSAL, by its Spanish acronym). We analysed 513,530 records of oncological care and performed chi-squared tests to examine the association between different cancer types and other characteristics, comparing observed data with expected proportions of different cancer services. Through a comprehensive analysis of these variables, we aim to uncover patterns and associations that can inform health policy and resource allocation, and ultimately contribute to better cancer prevention and treatment strategies in Peru. This study highlights the critical interplay of data science to provide insights and inform public health strategies regarding structural inequalities that have serious health consequences in Peruvian society.

articleTitle: Vivaldi Antipodal Slotted Antennas Design for Brain Anomaly Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The use of antennas in brain anomaly detection systems has been one of the most researched areas in recent years, yielding significant results and providing more accessible and less expensive portable equipment. Also, current proposals for integrated sensing and communications systems (ISAC) aim to simultaneously use spectrum for communications and sensing of the biological and environmental surroundings. At the same time, brain sensing systems use wide bandwidths to detect anomalies with higher resolution and hence accuracy. This poses the challenge of determining the most suitable antenna whose characteristics allow its implementation in sensing systems, featuring small size, unidirectional radiation and wide spectral performance to provide better sensing of the medium under test (MUT). In this paper, four Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna (AVA) designs are proposed, with increasing complexity aimed at reducing their size and optimizing their performance through techniques such as dielectric lens and slot aggregation. Measurements were performed on a phantom with permittivity values and anomalies associated with brain tissue, highlighting the antenna's ability to detect changes in the MUT spectrum. The results mainly highlight the sensors' performance for viable use in brain anomaly detection and sensing systems, demonstrating a maximum unidirectional gain of up to 11.8 dBi, wide operating frequency ranges of up to 10 GHz and miniaturised sizes of up to 45 mm x 38 mm.

articleTitle: Blockchain Based Data Transfer and Protection Framework for SMEs in Metropolitan Lima
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) are vital for Peru's economic development. However, they are among the most vulnerable to cybersecurity threats due to their usually inadequate or non-existent information security management systems. This research presents a reference framework that materializes a conceptual model for the use of blockchain technology to improve the security of sensitive data management in these organizations. The proposed architecture uses a cloud infrastructure that allows leveraging the properties of encryption, transparency, and easy auditing. For information storage and transfer processes, the principles of a Zero Trust architecture were maintained to maximize privacy and security in the company's infrastructure. The proposal was validated by determining the satisfaction of cybersecurity specialists and experts with the proposed technology on the relevance and effectiveness of the model. The final level of satisfaction obtained was 76.67%, demonstrating that the project met its objective according to the evaluation of the stakeholders.

articleTitle: Smart Shopping Carts: Reducing Checkout Queues with RFID and AWS Facial Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study evaluates the efficiency of an experimental checkout system compared to traditional supermarket checkout processes through trials conducted during low and high activity periods. The experimental system demonstrated significant efficiency improvements, reducing checkout times by approximately 73% during low activity and 84% during high activity. Survey data revealed that younger users (18–30 years) rated the UI (User Interface) friendliness highest at 8.70 and showed a 100% preference for the new system, experiencing fewer facial recognition issues and finding product offers largely relevant. Conversely, older users (51–70 years) preferred traditional systems, faced more facial recognition challenges, and rated the UI friendliness lower. These findings suggest the new system is effective and well-received by younger users but requires enhancements to better accommodate older users, underscoring its potential to improve the overall shopping experience while highlighting areas for broader acceptance.

articleTitle: AI Chatbot with Emotional Recognition for an Improved Customer Service Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In the telecommunications sector, customer dissatisfaction with automated service systems is a significant issue, as these systems often fail to effectively respond to users' emotional needs. This study presents the development and implementation of an intelligent chatbot designed to address this challenge by improving customer service through emotional recognition using advanced text mining and artificial intelligence techniques. The chatbot provides fast, accurate, and personalized responses, reducing wait times and enhancing the customer experience. To assess its effectiveness, a case study was conducted at SOE INDUSTRIAL E.I.R.L., collecting qualitative and quantitative data through post-conversation surveys and interaction logs. The objective was to understand the chatbot's impact in a real-world customer service environment. During the initial trial period, a significant improvement in customer satisfaction was observed, with an average customer experience score of 4.66 out of 5. The average response time was recorded at 2993.98 milliseconds, and the first-contact resolution rate was 68.97%. Considering reinteractions on the same issue, a total effectiveness rate of 86.21% was achieved. These results demonstrate that the chatbot is effective in improving service and consultation processes in the telecommunications sector.

articleTitle: Development of a Video Game for Teaching Good Project Management Practices to Undergraduate Students, Using the Agile Scrum Methodology and Gamification Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The project management challenge lies in bridging the gap between academic theory and practical application, a divide magnified by educational methods that inadequately prepare student teams for today's workplace. This research proposes an immersive learning 3D video game incorporating the Scrum framework and gamification principles as a solution. The approach fosters practical project management skills by enabling users to integrate theoretical knowledge through simulated tasks. It transcends traditional education limitations by aligning with current trends and emerging technologies, aiming to equip students and professionals with the ability to implement best practices in real-world settings. Preliminary results show enhanced understanding of the Scrum framework and increased engagement, leading to robust preparation for professional challenges. Future directions include conducting longitudinal studies to assess long-term impact, expanding the game to cover other agile methodologies, and exploring AI integration to further enhance the learning experience and its real-world applicability.

articleTitle: INSPIRA: Telemonitoring System for Patients with Acute and Chronic Respiratory Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Respiratory failure diseases have historically caused high mortality worldwide. Telemedicine emerged as a response to combat the high demand and healthcare overload, especially driven by the COVID-19 pandemic. However, current systems and equipment remain insufficient to achieve comprehensive monitoring of various respiratory pathologies. This project proposes an application for remote and comprehensive monitoring of patients with respiratory failure. The solution includes a wearable device that measures multiple physiological variables and performs specific tests, recording the data in a web interface for subsequent analysis by the specialist doctor. The main objective is to improve patient health management, facilitate communication between patient and doctor, allow early diagnosis and offer continuous monitoring of respiratory disease.

articleTitle: Retrospective Analysis of Hospitalization Patterns in Peru: Insights on Inpatient Resource Utilization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study addresses the inequality in hospital resource distribution in Peru using Data Mining techniques. Analyzing hospitalization data from 2018 to 2022, we employed K-means, Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) to identify patterns in hospital resource availability and inpatient service demand across different regions. Our findings reveal significant disparities, with resources concentrated in high-population urban areas, particularly Lima, and a predominance of public sector healthcare provision in inpatient settings. We identified potential saturation issues in departments like Lima and Arequipa, and substantial geographical discrepancies between inpatient care demand and hospital resource availability. Based on these insights, we propose targeted interventions to improve equity in hospital resource distribution, including resource redistribution and strengthening private sector capacity in underserved areas. This research provides valuable information for hospital policy planning and contributes to the broader goal of achieving equitable access to inpatient care in Peru.

articleTitle: Design and Manufacture of a Vital Signs Monitor with Real-Time Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The article presents the design and development of a vital signs monitor for use in ambulances, focusing on real-time data transmission capabilities. The device measures temperature, blood oxygen saturation (SpO2), and electrical heart activity (ECG) using an ESP32 microcontroller, which processes and transmits this information to the hospital emergency room through a web server hosted on the AWS cloud using the HTTP protocol. The methodological process included the electronic design, mechanical structure, signal processing and user interface development. Validation tests were conducted using biological signal simulators to ensure accuracy and reliability. The results showed a high level of precision in measuring all parameters, complying with the standards required for emergency medical devices.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Analysis and Risk Profiling of Dengue in Lima and Callao: A Data-Driven Approach for Tailored Prevention Policies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The recent atypical increase in dengue cases in Lima and Callao, Peru, underscores the need for a more sophisticated approach to controlling this disease in urban settings. This study employs advanced data mining techniques to conduct a comprehensive spatio-temporal analysis of dengue cases in these regions, integrating climatic, sanitation, and demographic factors at the district level. Using k-means clustering, two distinct risk profiles were identified among the districts, revealing spatial patterns related to port proximity and exposure to geological risks. Sensitivity analysis using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) quantified the contribution of various variables to dengue incidence, highlighting the importance of exposure to geological risks and water management practices. The results indicate that, contrary to previous assumptions, coastal humidity is not a determining factor in the spread of dengue in the region. Instead, factors such as wind speed, landslide exposure, and water conservation practices emerged as significant predictors. Based on these findings, the study proposes specific recommendations for dengue prevention policies tailored to district risk profiles. This data-driven approach to understanding and mitigating dengue in complex urban areas offers a potentially applicable model to other regions facing similar challenges in vector-borne disease control.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Hybrid Vehicle for Exploration of Risks in Underground Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This work presents the mechanical design and 3D simulation of an unmanned land-air hybrid vehicle capable of performing routine exploration tasks, remotely controlled by an operator. The vehicle is designed to assess the dangers present in underground mining, particularly focusing on the high accident rate associated with exploration projects. Routine inspections require capabilities such as detecting potential hazards, including poor ventilation indicated by low oxygen levels, high radiation levels caused by toxic gases such as radon, and the risk of landslides and collapses within the mine. The mechanical design comprises a terrestrial steering module, ground movement system, flight module, and the integration of these components. For the electronic system, sensors and actuators are selected for navigation in challenging environments and data acquisition. The control system includes a direction control strategy and a flight control loop.

articleTitle: Technological Model for the Prevention of Leaks of Medical Records Based on Blockchain Technology in the Peruvian Health Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This document proposes a technological model for the Peruvian health sector, which uses blockchain technology, IPFS and smart contracts to protect and ensure secure access to medical records. The model addresses the rise of health data breaches, identifies limitations of current approaches, and presents a new approach divided into four phases. It uses IPFS for decentralized information storage and a consensus algorithm for fast transactions.

articleTitle: Proof of Concept: A TinyML-Based Image Classifier for Detecting Microplastics and Waste in Simulated Marine Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study presents the development of an image classifier designed to identify microplastics and cardboard waste, with potential application in marine environments, using Tiny Machine Learning (TinyML) implemented on an ESP32-CAM module. A total of 229 images were collected, classified into mi-croplastics and non-microplastics, and preprocessing techniques such as scaling (to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$96\times 96$</tex> pixels) and normalization were applied to optimize the performance of the chosen model. The learning technique used was Transfer Learning, employing a model based on the MobileNetV1 architecture. The model was trained and validated, achieving an accuracy of 91.7% on the validation set under controlled conditions. This implementation demonstrates the initial feasibility of using TinyML on resource-constrained devices for plastic waste detection, laying the groundwork for future testing in real marine environments. The study provides a promising foundation for the development of environmental monitoring tools, although additional validation in field conditions is required to confirm its effectiveness in real aquatic ecosystems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Calibration Techniques for Low-Cost Particulate Matter Monitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study advances the field of low-cost air quality sensor calibration by integrating sophisticated machine learning techniques with time series analysis. We combine advanced algorithms such as Support Vector Regression (SVR) and Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) with SARIMA models to improve calibration accuracy across various sensor types and particulate matter sizes. Our Comprehensive approach reveals the superiority if ensemble methods incorporating SA RIMA components and highlights the varying performance of algorithms across different sensor types and particulate matter sizes. Key findings include the critical importance of temporal features and the persistent challenge in PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> calibration compared to PM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.5</inf>. The results underscore the potential of hybrid approaches that leverage both machine learning and time series analysis, enhancing calibration accuracy and model generalizability across diverse environmental conditions. This work contributes to the development of more reliable and accessible air quality monitoring systems, with significant implications for public health and environmental management.

articleTitle: A Survey on Large Language Models for Motion Generation from Text
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Over these last years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have evolved as an ubiquitous tool for different applications. One of those rapidly growing applications is motion generation, traditionally performed by a specific human design. This paper provides an overview of how motion is generated from text with the use of Large Language Models, targeted at 3D human representations and robots. We describe the different methodologies and techniques of the most used architectures, and the motion generation process in order to achieve the final motion. This survey aims to provide a comprehensive resource for researchers and developers seeking to leverage the power of LLMs to bridge the gap between text understanding and motion generation.

articleTitle: Modeling, Simulation, Design and Comparative Analysis of the PID and LQR Controllers for an Inverted Pendulum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The inverted pendulum is a classic nonlinear unstable system used in control theory for testing control methods. In this article a nonlinear and a linearized model is obtained to design a PID and LQR controller. The MATLAB®/Simulink® software is used for linear and nonlinear model simulation and controller design. WEBOTS software is used for implementation and for comparative analysis between the controllers performance using the standard deviation of the tilt angle and cart position, and the RMS value of the force applied to the cart as performance indices. To validate the robustness of each controller the system is tested against disturbances and reference changes in the cart position. The results of this study show that the LQR controller has minimum steady-state error and a smooth control signal. Nonetheless, according to the performance indices, the PID controller performs better than the LQR, with a position standard deviation of 0.0903m, angle standard deviation of 0.0120 rad and RMS value of the control signal of 1.1007N.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptation of Software Services Based on User Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In recent years, several methods have been proposed to evaluate user experience (UX) improvements using real-time emotion detection, but the correlation between user emotions and personality traits in self-adaptive software has not been fully explored. This paper investigates the feasibility of implementing a software service that adapts based on the user's emotional and personality state. Using pre-trained models for real-time emotion detection and the BFI-2-S test for personality assessment, we conducted an experiment with 30 users on the Neo Digital Skills platform, evaluated through the User Experience Question-naire (UEQ). Our findings show that self-adaptation significantly enhances UX, with improvements in Attractiveness (from -0.81 to 1.69), Stimulation (from -0.73 to 1.78), and Novelty (from - 0.62 to 2.02), indicating that personalization based on emotions and personality traits boosts user engagement, satisfaction, and innovation perceptions.

articleTitle: Application of the Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method in Presence of Dispersive Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method is a popular numerical approach for solving Maxwell's equations in the time domain. While the FDTD method has been extensively applied to calculate propagation of electromagnetic waves in non-dispersive media, its application in the presence of dispersive materials presents additional challenges. Dispersive media, such as dielectrics and plasmas, exhibit frequency-dependent permit-tivity, which must be accurately accounted for in the FDTD formulation. This paper presents a study of the implementation of the FDTD method for modeling wave propagation in Transverse Magnetic (TM) mode, in the presence of dispersive media, considering the Total Field/Scattered Field (TF /SF) technique. The paper also investigates the use of the Drude model, and demonstrates how changing the temperature of the dispersive medium can modify its permittivity. Simulation results, using a Gaussian source, for a two-dimensional cylindrical geometry are presented. These results demonstrate the FDTD method's capability to accurately capture the medium's dispersive proper-ties, including the temperature-dependent permittivity variations described by the Drude model.

articleTitle: Integration of Deep Learning Models and Explanatory Models to Detect Anomalous Periods in Vital Signs of Mining Truck Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: “Latex The Peruvian mining industry is beginning to adopt IoT technologies. The increasing complexity of modern engines makes it crucial to implement predictive maintenance systems to ensure reliability and performance optimization. This study is based on data obtained from an open-pit copper mine in southern Peru. The use of advanced machine learning models is proposed, evaluating between Long Short-Term Memory with Autoencoders (LSTM-AE) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) for anomaly detection in multivariate time series for diesel engine health monitoring. This project addresses three issues of the current analysis methodology: first, point anomalies are used to monitor potential failures, generating a high rate of false alarms, while the proposed method identifies abnormal time periods; second, the threshold for alerts is manually calculated and requires expert intervention periodically, whereas the proposed methodology calculates the threshold in an unsupervised manner. Third, deep learning models are often considered “black box” models since it is not easy to interpret how the model reached a conclusion, which is why model explainability is important for its adoption within the industry. The objective is to develop a predictive model that identifies potential failures early, allowing for the planning of preventive maintenance and reducing unplanned downtime. The results show that the combination of these models significantly improves the accuracy in failure prediction, facilitating timely and precise interventions.

articleTitle: Voice Recognition Acquisition and Storage System using VHDL and the DE1-SoC FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a voice acqui-sition and recognition system in VHDL, mainly optimized for FPGA DE1-SoC. The system implements advanced digital signal processing techniques combined with classification through the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm. The system operates at a 320 kHz sampling rate, with a latency of 10 ns and power consumption of 1.2 W. The design enhances precision and noise rejection through the use of Hamming windows and integer-based processing. Future improvements will focus on the implementation of neural networks to replace the KNN algorithm and further increase system accuracy.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Analyzing $(CO_{2})$ Concentrations and Vegetation Health in Lima, Peru Using Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Climate change, driven significantly by carbon diox-ide (CO2) emissions, poses a major threat globally, contributing to extreme weather events and health impacts. This study focuses on Lima, Peru, a city facing severe air pollution, to monitor and analyze CO2 concentrations using satellite imagery. By leveraging Sentinel-2 and OCO-3 data, we examine the relationship between CO2 levels and vegetation health, using vegetation indices such as NDVI. Our findings reveal temporal variability in these relationships, underscoring the complex interactions between atmospheric CO2 and possible vegetation influenced by seasonal and environmental factors. The study recommends increasing the frequency of satellite observations and integrating these findings with climate models to improve urban green space management and climate change mitigation strategies. This approach enhances spatial and temporal resolution of CO2 data, facilitating informed decision-making for environmental and public health interventions.

articleTitle: Dispersion analysis of the energy consumption and carbon footprint of photovoltaic energy use through design of experiments (DOE)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study investigated the environmental impact and energy performance of first-generation poly-Si photovoltaic (PV) systems in Peru through the application of design of experiments (DOE) techniques. The objective of this article was to analyze the environmental impact of these PV systems through the evaluation of their life cycle, considering the degree of dispersion of the variables required for the calculation of energy consumption at each stage of the life cycle and those that influence the energy generation process. Two DOE methods were employed to calculate the energy payback time (EPBT) and carbon footprint for two different cases: five rural households in Puno and the Rubi Solar Plant. The results indicate consistency across both cases, with the Face Centered Central Composite Design (CCD) method providing a more realistic description of dispersion due to the linear equation nature of the EPBT calculation. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for diverse factors in PV system analysis for accurate environmental impact and energy performance assessments.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Wireless Network in the Peruvian Amazon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article describes the implementation and performance of a long-distance wireless data network to provide Internet access service to public institutions located in the villages of the Santiago River basin (Amazon - Perú). In 2018, the regional Amazon Broadband project did not include these villages in its plans, leaving them without Internet access, and thus worsening the economic and social development of these communities. To solve this problem, a multi-stakeholder alliance was formed between public institutions and the university to develop a project that consisted of designing and implementing a broadband connectivity solution for the Santiago River basin. This multi-stakeholder alliance is an innovative model for solving various social problems in Peru. From a technical standpoint, the project's objective is to validate the use of unlicensed band wireless technology as an economical and feasible solution to be used as a backhaul for providing Internet access solutions in disadvantaged rural areas. The design and implementation of this data network was developed by GTR-PUCP (Pontifical Catholic University of Perú) with the aim of improving the quality of life and economic growth of these villages, and it could be replicated in other scenarios where private companies have no interest. Currently, the Santiago River network is completed and is used by around 200 users on a working day, who use the Internet, video conferencing, VoIP communication, and telehealth. The success of the network has aroused the interest of private telecommunications companies that wish to use the network to provide mobile phone services in exchange for maintaining the network, thus demonstrating that it is possible to contribute to closing the digital divide.

articleTitle: Development of a Mobile Application Based on a Machine Learning Model to Identify Potential Cases of Smartphone Addiction in School-Aged Adolescents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The pervasiveness of digital devices, especially smartphones, has heightened concerns regarding smartphone addiction among adolescents. This study aims to develop a mobile application that utilizes a high-precision machine learning (ML) model to identify smartphone addiction cases in school-aged adolescents. The ML model, trained using a logistic regression algorithm, uses a dataset of 308 adolescent records. The dataset includes sociodemographic data, smartphone addiction status, and responses based on the short version of the Smartphone Addiction Scale (SAS-SV). The model achieved an accuracy of 92%, indicating its effectiveness in identifying smartphone addiction cases. The Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.998 and the F1 score of 0.931 further indicate the model's strong performance. The integration of the ML model into an Android mobile application facilitates accessibility and usability for both parents and adolescents. The application provides real-time results, enabling timely intervention and preventive measures. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of ML in identifying smartphone addiction in adolescents. The mobile application offers a valuable tool for parents, educators, and healthcare professionals to address this growing concern. Future work aims to enhance the model's accuracy and expand the application's functionalities.

articleTitle: UAV Onboard Hotspot Detection using a Lightweight Thermal Camera and Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The analysis of a hotspot is a critical issue in mitigating natural disasters such as forest fires and volcanic eruptions. UAVs can be used to monitor a hotspot using manual navigation. However, there is a risk to operators during the natural disaster. In this research, a navigation algorithm is developed to strategically position itself over a hotspot. In the experimental results, the automatic navigation of the drone has a maximum error of 1.7 m with respect to the hotspot and has a duration of 30 s-. This automated approach not only improves the safety of UA Voperators, but also provides an accurate method for positioning over a hot spot, paving the way for applications in automated surveillance and disaster response systems.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Convolutional Neural Networks for Oregano Diseases Classification in A Novel Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Peru is South America's largest producer and ex-porter of oregano (Origanum vulgare L.), with the Tacna region being the most significant contributor, cultivating 2,499 hectares and producing 11,946 tons, accounting for 65% of the national production. To mitigate the impact of oregano diseases, which lead to substantial crop losses and negatively affect the economy, it is crucial to develop and upgrade technologies for disease management. Accurate classification of oregano diseases can prevent quality deterioration and yield reductions. However, the availability of data and the use of advanced technologies in oregano cultivation are still in their early stages. This study addresses these shortcomings by developing and publishing a novel public dataset for the classification of the most common oregano diseases-Alternaria, Powdery Mildew (Oidium), and Mosaic-using crops from Susapaya - Tarata in Tacna, Peru.
