To classify oregano diseases, we conducted a comprehensive comparative study, applying Transfer Learning and Fine-Tuning techniques to evaluate the performance of VGG16, MobileNet, MobileNetV2, and NasNetLarge architectures with modifications in the classifier. The experiments revealed that: (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i$</tex>) Fine-Tuning improved validation set accuracy by 4.47% compared to Transfer Learning, (ii) the VGG16 architecture achieved the highest accuracy at 0.993921, (iii) MobileNet and MobileNetV2 models performed similarly, (iv) the NASNetLarge model showed poor performance when only Transfer Learning was applied, and (v) there was a strong significant relationship <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R^{2}=\mathbf{0.84})$</tex> between the number of parameters and size (in MB) with the performance of the architectures on our dataset. We ensure the reproducibility of the results by making the novel dataset and the best model publicly available on GitHub.

articleTitle: Identification and Estimation of the Taylor Cone in Electrospinning Technique Using the Yolo Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Nanoscience and nanotechnology are revolutionizing various scientific and industrial fields by exploring materials at the nanoscale. This study focuses on the electro spinning process of nanofibers, essential in the manufacture of medical textiles, ceramics, and other products. The “Taylor Cone,” a visible phenomenon under high electrical field, is important for evaluating the quality of electrospinning. This article presents a method to geometrically identify and estimate the Taylor Cone using process images captured in the electronics laboratory of the School of Physics at the National University of Trujillo. Experimental parameters included a power source of 0–12 kVolts and an 8 cm distance to the collector plate. The dataset was categorized into “Ausencia,” “Formacion,” and “Cono_Taylor.” Using Yolov8n after 150 epochs, a reliability of 70% in predictions was achieved. Results showed precision rates of 88.24 %, 70.3%, and 76.62%, with recalls of 84.5%, 100%, and 84.5%. Corresponding F1-scores were 86.33%, 82.56%, and 79.68%. The overall accuracy was 77.24%. For geometric estimation, an image from the “Formacion” class revealed a Taylor Cone height of 0.9 mm, a radius of 0.35 mm, and angles measured at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23.776^\circ,60.113^\circ$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$96.111^{\circ}$</tex> for the cone vertices. This study highlights the effectiveness of Yolov8n in detecting and characterizing the Taylor Cone, thereby enhancing the precision and efficiency of electrospinning in nanotechnology and biomedicine applications.

articleTitle: Project Finance and Asset Management for Electric Transmission Lines in Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper is focused on the technical, regulatory, and financial evaluation of the electricity transmission service that a company can provide to an electricity generation company for the electric transmission lines services for a period of 30 years. The analysis includes the regulatory context and the role that each regulatory institution plays when evaluating a project of this large scale. This paper also describes asset management practices for the transmission lines that need to be considered when contracting the electricity transmission service. This paper additionally entails the regulatory frame for a hydroelectric power plant in Peru and the economic, technical, and financial factors that the company needs to consider when they want to connect their plant to a substation in the National Interconnected Electrical System (SEIN).

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Classifier Algorithms for Electric Load Disaggregation Based on Average Power Signatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) systems disaggregate energy consumption data to provide insights into appliance-level usage. This study addresses the challenge of accurately estimating energy consumption using machine learning algorithms, particularly with low-frequency data. We propose a simplified NILM methodology based on time windows to reduce computational load and enhance efficiency. This method extracts features using power centroids and binary coding for labeling, making it suitable for resource-constrained devices. We evaluate the performance of six machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest Classifier (RFC), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting (GB), and Support Vector Machines (SVM), using the Reference Energy Disaggregation Dataset (REDD). Our results demonstrate that RFC and SVC outperform other models in classifying and predicting electrical power, especially with imbalanced datasets. This research contributes to the development of practical NILM solutions for promoting energy efficiency in residential settings

articleTitle: Digital Education Platform with Interactive Curricular Content for Public Schools in Rural Peru
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, the education system in Peru was severely affected. The need to adopt digital education has become critical. However, most Peruvian schools have struggled to adapt due to a lack of access to educational platforms and appropriate content. To solve this problem, it is necessary to find a solution that allows the delivery of curricular content despite having limited internet connectivity. A digital education platform is proposed to enhance the quality of education in Peru, allowing students to access curriculum content and teachers to create interactive courses to further motivate their students. The platform will also include a peer-to-peer communication system. This will allow content to be shared with other users within the same network. In areas with limited internet connectivity, this will maximize access to digital education. The solution has been tested in a public school in a rural region with poorer internet access. This solution is expected to be implemented throughout the country in all Peruvian schools to improve the quality of education in the country.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of AWS IoT Connected Dataloggers in Glacier Environments: Campbell CR1000X vs. ESP32 Open Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Monitoring hydrometeorological conditions in high mountain areas is crucial for understanding and mitigating the impacts of climate change. This study addresses the development and implementation of both commercial and open-source data-loggers for weather monitoring in these environments. Through a review of the hardware and software used, we present the tools employed in the development of the study, along with the network infrastructure that connects the city of Huaraz with Lake Palcacocha, enabling internet access, as well as the IoT network design for each datalogger. The commercial datalogger was configured according to the manufacturer's guidelines, establishing secure MQTT communication with AWS IoT Core. On the other hand, the open-source datalogger required the development of custom scripts in the Arduino IDE, incorporating WiFi and MQTT libraries, and overcoming challenges related to network reconnection and data integrity. Field experiments demonstrated high data transmission efficiency (commercial: 99.68%, open-source: 99.69%). Although the open-source data-logger required code tuning to achieve performance comparable to the commercial version, it proved viable as an open-source solution for high-altitude monitoring. Compatibility with AWS IoT Core enabled real-time data visualization, storage, and enhanced responsiveness to extreme weather events.

articleTitle: Architectural Model Based on TOGAF to Attend to the Admission of Families in a Shelter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In the temporary homes context, efficiency in managing the intake process is crucial, and the lack of an appropriate business architecture can lead to inefficiencies and errors. Therefore, this study focuses on developing and implementing a specific enterprise architecture for these organizations, focusing on enrollment management. A detailed analysis of the current enrollment process will be conducted to identify areas of improvement and key needs. Based on these findings, an enterprise architecture will be designed and implemented that streamlines the admission process. It is expected to reduce the admission problem by 40% with this new architecture, improving both operational efficiency and the user experience and quality of life of residents. This solution will not only optimize times and reduce errors but will also facilitate the work of assistants in these social centers, serving as a model for future similar projects in other areas.

articleTitle: Predicting System for Nosocomial Infections in Peruvian Public Hospitals using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE XXXI International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: One of the most important challenges for public health systems in Peru is the control of Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAI), which has had a high economic and social impact in recent years. Due to the limited resources available in the health sector, it is critical to find solutions to strengthen medical surveillance and have valuable information that allows for timely decision-making. In this context, artificial intelligence (AI) systems, consisting of logical algorithms trained to make decisions, offer alternatives to improve medical management by predictive models implemented in different scenarios. This applied research proposes the implementation of an HAI prediction system using artificial neural networks. The proposed system was developed in a five-layer architecture: capture, logic, training, storage, and presentation. The validation process for the proposal was carried out in three phases: selection, registration, and training. Two experiments were conducted, for which data from two and three weeks were taken from eight hospitals belonging to the Social Health Insurance of Peru. Additionally, with the support of experts, the results were evaluated, this demonstrated that the system allows for the prediction of HAI's based on the fourteen selected variables with values above 95% in each metric, reaching sensitivity values of 99.1%, specificity of 99.6%, and AUROC of 99.2%.
